node.title: C36' rich product fibers are confined below the 6^(n/4) norm threshold
node.statement: For n=2^s, p=1 mod n, H of order n, A=(1-H)\{0}, and P(t)=#{(a,b) in A^2:ab=t}, one has P(t)>=19 only if p<=6^(n/4). Ten unordered representations forced by P>=19 yield ten odd-conjugate coefficient vectors. At most two are diagonal and at most one contains -1, so at least seven have squared norm at most 3. The seven-vector centroid identity forces a pair at squared distance at most 6. Parseval and AM-GM give a nonzero collision obstruction of norm at most 6^(n/4). Thus X_18=0 for p>6^(n/4), reducing the open C36' range to n^2<=p<=6^(n/4).
